title: History's Greatest Mysteries
description:
Houdini's Lost Diaries
Harry Houdini left behind a diary that had been kept from the public, held under lock and key by a wealthy New York City Family. Now, magician and Houdini expert Bill Kalush has finally secured access to these pages.

title: History's Greatest Mysteries
description:
The Holy Grail
It's a treasure coveted by everyone from Roman Emperors to Adolf Hitler--a sacred object said to hold incredible powers of healing, resurrection, and immortality. It may be the world's most sought-after relic, but what is the Holy Grail?

title: History's Greatest Mysteries
description:
The Amber Room
One of World War II's greatest unsolved mysteries: an incomparable work of art worth half a billion dollars, lost without a trace. Where is the famed Amber Room? And will a brand-new search finally reveal its true location?

title: History's Greatest Mysteries
description:
Hunting Hitler's U-Boats
Decades before his death in 2018, Roger believed he discovered a modified Nazi U-boat loaded with a fortune in artwork, antiquities, and gold off the coast of Turks and Caicos.

title: History's Greatest Mysteries
description:
Expedition Bermuda Triangle
No ship in history has searched the extreme depths of the Bermuda Triangle, thought to have claimed over 1,000 ships and planes, until now. The R/V Petrel, the most advanced search vessel of its kind, will try.

title: Biography
description:
Cat Stevens
The world knew him as Cat Stevens, an artist whose songs conquered the hearts of a generation. But after selling over 40 million records, he turned his back on the music industry, mystifying his fans. Since then, Cat Stevens' search for his own identity has taken him on an extraordinary journey, and has led him to a religion often times misunderstood: Islam. In a world of fear, his effort to create a greater understanding of his faith has often times met controversy. After nearly two decades away, he is back fighting to spread his message of peace through music.

title: Biz Kids
description:
The Global Economy
Go around the world with the Biz Kid$! Join us, and you’ll follow the flow of imports and exports that make up the interconnected world economy. You’ll also see how several entrepreneurs have relied on the global economy to build a successful business.  Meet the filmmakers for the movie 'Outsourced' and find out what it was like to bridge the distance between India and America.

title: Biz Kids
description:
Bulls, Bears, and Financial Markets
Kids and bulls and bears, oh my! The Biz Kid$ examine stocks, bonds, commodities, and the markets where they are traded. You'll discover various ways young people can get involved with the transactions, aim for profit, and avoid risk. Meet a 12-year-old investing guru who teaches adults about the stock market, and a young woman who's already investing in her retirement.

title: Missing: Cold Cases
description:
Missing: Cold Case 273
Profiling the cold cases of missing children; Internet safety tips; Advice for children and teens about emergency contacts and safety skills.

title: Missing: Cold Cases
description:
Missing: Cold Case 274
Profiling the cold cases of missing children; Internet safety tips; Advice for children and teens about emergency contacts and safety skills.

title: Biography
description:
Johnny Cash
Rags-to-riches story of the son of a poor cotton farmer who learned guitar while serving in the Air Force during the Korean War. Without musical education, he rose to the top of the country-western world and proved himself an accomplished actor in several films. Highlights include interviews with daughter Rosanne and rock star Tom Petty.

title: Story Feature
description:
Dolly Parton: Big Hair, Bigger Heart
No royal beginnings for this Queen of Country Music, Dolly Parton. Known for her larger-than-life positive attitude parading big hair and bold make-up, she would later carve out her own identity as a singer, composer, movie actress, and entrepreneur. Despite dirt poor roots, Dolly Parton leaves a rich legacy.

title: Biography
description:
Kris Kristofferson
Songwriter, singer, actor, Rhodes scholar, army captain, helicopter pilot, and sex symbol! Follow the ups and downs of Kris Kristofferson's career, and listen again to his famous songs. Willie Nelson, Waylon Jennings, and Kris's ex-wife and daughters offer private views of this counter-culture hero.

title: Biography
description:
Garth Brooks: The Road I'm On (Part 1)
This "Biography" special offers an intimate look into Brooks' life as a musician, father, and man, as well as the moments that have defined his decades-spanning career and seminal hit songs.

title: Perspectives
description:
George Bernard Shaw
Playwright, philosopher, and egotist--these are some of the fascinating parts that made up one of the 20th century's most celebrated dramatists.

title: Perspectives
description:
Helen Keller
The revered humanitarian is interviewed for this moving story of a remarkable woman's rise from blindness to greatness as a speaker and world traveler.

title: Biography
description:
Helen Thomas: First Lady of the Press
Profile of the legendary White House reporter who broke ground for women in journalism and who has kept presidents on the defensive with her probing questions and coverage.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Operation Jawbreaker
Just fifteen days after September 11th, 2001, CIA operatives land in Afghanistan with suitcases full of cash and a mission to dismantle the Taliban.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Operation Just Cause
During the presidency of George H.W. Bush, the United States invaded Panama to depose its de facto ruler, Manuel Noriega.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Operation Pimlico
A Soviet double agent requests extraction from Moscow. MI-6 orchestrates a daring escapade to retrieve him before his cover is blown.

title: Spy Ops
description:
The Plot to Kill the Pope
A stunning testimony from a man who planned and attempted an assassination of Catholicism's highest figure, Pope John Paul II.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Operation Wrath of God (Part I)
Mossad carries out a covert assassination campaign targeting leaders of the Popular Front to Liberate Palestine, Fatah, and other Palestinian movements.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Operation Wrath Of God (Part II)
Mossad continues its campaign of covert assassinations of Palestinian leaders, including car bombs and amphibious operations.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Taliban Spies
A look at how the US military's complex operations in Afghanistan required the collaboration of locals for cultural and strategic insights.

title: Spy Ops
description:
Project Azorian
At the height of the Cold War, the US military endeavors to recover a sunken Soviet submarine from the depths of the ocean floor.

description:

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Saltbox
In this episode, builder Marty Dunham heads to Connecticut. In Norwich, he examines the peculiar layout of a 300-year-old Saltbox house. And the woodchips fly as he fires up the chainsaw and helps finish up some structural repairs.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Sears Home
In the early 1900s, buying a home was as simple as ordering it through the Sears catalog. Across the country over 75,000 Sears kit homes were built. Delivered in 30,000 pieces, they offered affordable and well-built housing to a growing middle class.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Spanish Revival
The Spanish Revival (or Spanish Colonial Revival) home takes cues from all over the Mediterranean, mixes those with pre-Columbian buildings, drops it over a conventional stick frame, and makes a uniquely American home.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Floating Home
More of our series focusing on historic houses. Today, host and contractor Marty Dunham helps restore and refloat the famous floating homes of Portland, Oregon.

title: The Big Build
description:
Lighthouse
Ever since sailors ventured into open waters, mariners have needed lighted signals to guide them safely through the night.

title: The Big Build
description:
Castle Tower
Our host, contractor Nick Mystrom, lands in Northern Idaho to erect a 2-story medieval castle tower in the same manner used by masons almost 1,000 years ago.

title: The Big Build
description:
Frontier Fort
Speed is the key word for this down-and-dirty build--Lewis and Clark, racing Oregon winter chill, built the 50 foot by 50 foot Fort Clatsop, a double-structure shelter with seven rooms, a sentry box, and parade ground, in just 15 days.

title: Boneyard
description:
Demolition
With America's cities and industrial centers rapidly aging and growing, thousands of buildings must be destroyed in order to be raised up again. These structures and their internal components will be transformed and recycled. There is great value not only in the structural materials, such as concrete, brick, and steel, but also in a wide array of vital, non-structural items like copper wire, stairways, plumbing, insulation, ventilation systems, and even glass. For many of the more grand structures, their hand-crafted and unique architectural features must be carefully removed and restored to new life. For all these activities there is a vast demolition industry to provide the expertise, skills, and the increasingly specialized tools to do the job.

title: Boneyard
description:
Garbage
The average American throws out more than four pounds of trash a day, nearly 300 million tons annually. An army of technologically advanced machines processes garbage, from the local collection trucks to the landfill compactors. In facilities called "Murfs," millions of tons of resources are given a second life. The water bottles you tossed in your recycling bin might become your new blanket. Electricity may be generated from the garbage you set out at your curb. Discover their unusual after-life as new products are created from garbage.

title: Story Feature
description:
The Big Dig
The Massachusetts Central Artery/Tunnel Project, a.k.a. The Big Dig, is the most amazing municipal construction project in U.S. history. Its objective--to replace Boston's decaying highway infrastructure with 160 new highway miles, half of which run underground and underwater. After 14 years construction, its cost--$11 billion!
